config.title: Cart Context

intro.title: Cart Context
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart context to manage product data and cart state across your Vue application. You'll learn how to use Vue's Composition API, specifically the `ref` and `provide`/`inject` functions, to create and share reactive state. This involves creating a centralized cart context that holds items and provides methods to add or remove them. By the end, you'll have a functional cart system that demonstrates state management in a beginner-friendly Vue project.
intro.usecase: Cart context is a fundamental pattern in e-commerce applications where multiple components need access to shared shopping cart data. You'll see this in product listings, cart summary widgets, checkout flows, and header cart indicators - all needing to display consistent cart information without prop drilling. For example, when a user adds an item from a product card, the cart icon in the navigation bar should immediately update the item count. This pattern also enables features like persistent carts across page navigation and real-time inventory synchronization across different UI sections.

objectives: Initialize a reactive cart state using Vue's ref or reactive
Construct a cart context provider to share state across components
Implement functions to add and remove items from the cart state
Bind cart data to UI components using computed properties
Integrate the cart context into a component to display cart items
Manipulate the cart state through user interactions like button clicks
Control cart item quantities with increment and decrement handlers

steps.title: Import Vue and createApp
steps.instruction: Import Vue and createApp from the Vue CDN or module to set up the foundation for your Vue application.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and createApp from the Vue package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing Vue and createApp
import { createApp } from 'vue'
steps.expectedOutcome: Vue and createApp are imported and ready to be used in the application.
successCriteria: Vue and createApp are imported from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both Vue and createApp from 'vue'.
steps.feedbackWrong: import Vue and createApp from the Vue module to proceed.

steps.title: Create a CartContext with provide and inject
steps.instruction: Create a CartContext object using Vue's provide and inject functions. Define it as a simple object with an empty array for items and a function to add items.
steps.hint: You can create a plain JavaScript object with properties like items and addItem. The provide/inject setup will come later.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Vue and createApp here

// Create CartContext object here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartContext object is defined with items array and addItem function.
successCriteria: CartContext is defined as an object with items (array) and addItem (function).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the CartContext object structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started, but make sure CartContext has both items array and addItem function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a CartContext object with items and addItem properties.

steps.title: Create CartProvider component
steps.instruction: Define a Vue component named CartProvider that returns a template with a single <slot> element.
steps.hint: Create a component that will wrap child components and provide them with cart context. Use the Vue component syntax with a template containing <slot>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CartProvider component is created that can wrap other components and provide cart state to them.
successCriteria: CartProvider component is defined with a template containing a <slot> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the component is named CartProvider and includes a template with a <slot> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CartProvider component isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a Vue component with the correct name and template structure.

steps.title: Initialize cart state with reactive
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component, initialize a cart state variable using Vue's reactive API. Create it as a reactive object with two properties: an empty array for items and a number for total set to 0.
steps.hint: Use const cart = reactive({ items: [], total: 0 }) to create the reactive cart state object.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component now has a reactive cart state object with items and total properties ready for use.
successCriteria: A cart variable is declared using reactive() with an object containing items (empty array) and total (0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using reactive() and including both items (array) and total (number) properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The cart state initialization is missing or incorrect. Use reactive() to create an object with items: [] and total: 0.

steps.title: Define addToCart handler
steps.instruction: Inside the CartProvider component's setup function, define a function named addToCart that takes an item object as a parameter.
steps.hint: You can define a function inside setup() using either function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component will have an addToCart function defined in its setup function, ready to implement cart logic in the next step.
successCriteria: The addToCart function is defined inside setup() with a parameter for the item.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you define a function named addToCart inside the setup() function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The addToCart function needs to be defined inside the CartProvider's setup function. Try creating a function with that name.

steps.title: Provide cart state and handlers via CartProvider
steps.instruction: In the CartProvider component's setup function, use Vue.provide to expose the cart state, addToCart, and removeFromCart to child components.
steps.hint: Call Vue.provide with a key (like 'cart') and an object containing the values you want to make available.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CartProvider component will make cart, addToCart, and removeFromCart available to any child component that injects them.
successCriteria: Vue.provide is called with a key and an object containing cart, addToCart, and removeFromCart.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to provide all three values: cart, addToCart, and removeFromCart.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the Vue.provide call. It should include a key and an object with the cart state and handlers.

steps.title: Create ProductList component
steps.instruction: Define a ProductList component that will display products and use cart context. Create it as a Vue component object with a setup function.
steps.hint: Start by declaring a constant named ProductList and assign it an object with a setup method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ProductList component object is created with a setup method, ready to consume cart context and display products.
successCriteria: ProductList component is defined as a constant with a setup method that returns an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined ProductList as a Vue component object with a setup method that returns something.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductList component isn't properly defined. It should be a constant assigned to an object with a setup method.

steps.title: Inject cart context in ProductList
steps.instruction: Inside the ProductList component, use Vue.inject to access the cart context (cart state and handlers).
steps.hint: Use Vue.inject('cart') to get the cart context object that was provided by CartProvider.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductList component will have access to the cart state and handlers via Vue.inject.
successCriteria: ProductList uses Vue.inject('cart') to retrieve the cart context in its setup function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using Vue.inject('cart') to get the context object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ProductList component needs to inject the cart context using Vue.inject('cart') in its setup function.

steps.title: Wire addToCart to product buttons
steps.instruction: In the ProductList component's template, add a button for each product that calls the injected addToCart handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Use v-for to iterate through products and v-on:click (or @click) to call addToCart with the current product.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Button with click handler
<button @click="addToCart(product)">Add to Cart</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ProductList component will display buttons that add products to the cart when clicked.
successCriteria: ProductList template contains buttons with click handlers that call addToCart.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure each button has a click handler that calls addToCart with the product.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly connected to the addToCart handler. Check the template syntax.
